Read and check a proof ledger

Source: R/ledger.R
ldgrread.Rd

A proof ledger records the theorems of a formal-proof build (Lean and Mathlib): each theorem's statement, file and line, its status (proved, sorry or axiom) and number of sorry placeholders, the package functions whose behaviour it states, and optionally a numeric check of one of them in R. The format is schemapath("ledger"), in the style of the capsule schemas; nothing in it is specific to this package, so any package can ship a ledger in inst/ledger/ and any formal-proof project can write one.

Usage

ldgrread(path)

# S3 method for class 'rmbl_ledger'
print(x, ...)

ldgrchk(ledger, pkgs = NULL)

Arguments

path

Character scalar, the ledger JSON file.

x

A ldgrread() result.

...

Not used.

ledger

A ldgrread() result, or the path of a ledger file.

pkgs

Character vector: check only the covered functions and checks of these packages; NULL (the default) checks every package named.

Value

ldgrread(): the ledger, a list of class rmbl_ledger, with the normalised path as the attribute path. ldgrchk(): a data frame with the columns capsule, part (ledger, or the capsule parts), file, check, ok, detail, severity (error, warn or note) and line.

Details

ldgrread() parses the file and validates it against the schema; a file that does not validate, or that repeats a theorem id, is refused with the first problems found.

ldgrchk() returns check rows in the shape of rmbl verify (the rows of cpschk()):

proved: ID

the theorem is proved with sorry_count 0. A sorry fails as an error; an axiom fails as a warning (it is assumed, not proved).

covered: ID PKG::FN

the covered function is exported by the installed package; a package that is not installed here is a note, not a failure (it cannot be checked).

check: ID

the theorem's check$expr evaluates within check$tol (default 1e-8) of check$expect. The expression is evaluated in a sandbox: an environment holding only the exported functions of the first R package the theorem covers and a short list of base arithmetic and constructors (c, list, seq, rep, sum, +, $, ...). Anything else is refused before evaluation: a call to any other function (system(), file(), eval(), another package), a free variable, or an expression whose outer call is not a call to that package (or an extraction from one). Evaluation is limited to 10 seconds.

ledger_commit_pinned, ledger_build_pinned

when the ledger is the data file of a capsule whose provenance says kind: "ledger": the provenance's source$commit and source$build_digest equal the ledger's. The capsule's own rows (vrfcps(), the bundle and attestation through cpsbndlvrf(), the schemas) come with them, as rmbl verify reports them; rmbl verify adds the ledger rows to such a capsule too.

See also

schemapath(), cpschk(), cpsbndlvrf().

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "ledger_sample.json", package = "rmoriebricklayer")
l <- ldgrread(f)
l
#> Proof ledger rmoriebricklayer sample ledger: 3 theorems (1 proved, 1 sorry, 1 axiom)
#>   https://github.com/rootcoder007/rmorie-proofs @ 0123456789ab, Lean v4.12.0
r <- ldgrchk(l)
r[, c("check", "ok", "severity", "detail")]
#>                                                check    ok severity
#> 1                                 proved: gini-equal  TRUE    error
#> 2     covered: gini-equal rmoriebricklayer::ginicoef  TRUE    error
#> 3                                  check: gini-equal  TRUE    error
#> 4                            proved: lorenz-monotone FALSE    error
#> 5 covered: lorenz-monotone rmoriebricklayer::lorenzc  TRUE    error
#> 6                                proved: float-round FALSE     warn
#>                                                 detail
#> 1             Rmorie.Gini.gini_const_eq_zero, no sorry
#> 2                    exported by the installed package
#> 3 ginicoef(c(5, 5, 5, 5)) = 0, expected 0 within 1e-12
#> 4    Rmorie.Gini.lorenz_monotone is sorry with 1 sorry
#> 5                    exported by the installed package
#> 6     Rmorie.Float.round_nearest is axiom with 0 sorry

# a file that is not a ledger
bad <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
writeLines('{"name": "x"}', bad)
try(ldgrread(bad))
#> Error : ldgrread: file1fc459cc3f41.json is not a ledger: $: missing required toolchain, source, theorems
unlink(bad)
